Prevention: Control weeds around the rice field before planting, especially wild rice, barnyard grass, jungle rice, wrinkle duck-beak (alternate hosts)
July-August or separate transplanting method 2 times per crop for reducing damage.
In outbreak areas don’t sow or transplant densely (recommend 25x25 cm for transplanting and 15- 20 kg/rai for direct seeding)
Don’t apply any insecticides especially granular formulations.
Insecticides are not effective and destroy or kill natural enemies of gall midge (larvae parasitoids: platygasterid, eupelmid, and pteromalid wasps; pupa parasitoids: eupelmid wasps.
Monitoring: RGM at lights along road side and home for adult
RGM In rice field, look for tubular gall during tillering stage
Direct Control: Use sticky board with oil next to home light to attract adult
